messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector rollout at 10:12 PT I’m seeing a ~15% p95 regression on the non-chat embeddings/rerank endpoint in staging. Repro steps in the thread below.
perf-bot: deploy redwood-runtime@canary -> stable promoted at 2026-03-17T17:12:03Z :rocket: (canary id: c-482)
maya: ack, can you paste the staging load pattern + a quick flame output? curious if this is batching or KV cache pressure.
alex: repro load is the standard vector-rerank synthetic: 1200 QPS for 60s, avg seq len 96 tokens, token budget target 512 (current). Attached pprof snapshot:
```
pprof top -lines -percent
10.8%  kernel_selector.SelectKernel
7.3%   execution.BatchCopyTokens
6.5%   kvcache.EvictCold
5.1%   batching.WindowSampler
4.8%   io.ReadShard
...
```
sam: interesting — kernel_selector is up ~10% in CPU time. Did the new selector prefer the AVX path that increases copy overhead for small sequences?
henry: Yes, the selector change biases toward bigger kernel tiles when estimated seq len >= 80. For short-ish sequences that results in extra memcpy to align buffers. We tuned it because of long-chat wins.
leah: that matches the token-copy lines. For non-chat rerank we typically would prefer micro-tiles to avoid the copy. We should consider a per-endpoint affinity in kernel selection.
maya: also seeing kvcache.EvictCold — check KVCACHE hit rate in the same run?
alex: hit-rate dropped from 92% -> 82% during the regression window. KV mem pressure goes up when batches form with more diverse prefixes (the new batching window is 30ms), which forces earlier eviction.
sam: so there are two interacting causes: kernel path choice increasing memcpy + batching window change increasing diverse prefixes -> lower KV hit -> more recompute. Compound effect explains p95.
henry: proposal: for rerank/emb endpoints (non-chat) we flip kernel-selector to favor micro-tiles when seq < 128 and enable a stricter coalescing policy in batching (coalesce on prefix similarity > 0.6). Run A/B in staging.
leah: add small change to continuous-batcher: decrease max window from 30ms -> 12ms for non-chat rerank and set token_budget_target from 512 -> 256 for embeddings-heavy workloads. Expect lower latency but possibly higher cost.
maya: can we run a quick smoke with these three toggles disabled/enabled and collect: p95 latency, KV hit-rate, CPU memcpy percent, and token/sec throughput?
alex: yes. I'm kicking off the canary with the following toggles:
```json
{
  "kernel_selector": {"micro_tile_bias_threshold": 128},
  "batcher": {"max_window_ms_nonchat": 12, "prefix_coalesce_threshold": 0.6},
  "token_budget": {"nonchat": 256}
}
```
perf-bot: experiment created: experiment/emb-nonchat-kv-kernel-coal (id: e-117). Traffic: 10% staging -> canary.
sam: measurement checklist: include KV hit timeline, batch size distribution, batch formation latency histogram, and a short trace (span-level) that shows kernel selection decisions.
leah: also collect Numa/affinity stats — AVX paths sometimes push weird memory layouts causing memcpy to spike.
maya: agreed. alex, can you paste the smoke results when ready and we'll decide whether to ship the selector rollback or the per-endpoint affinity?
alex: initial smoke (10% canary, 5 runs): p95 down from +15% -> +1.8% vs baseline; KV hit-rate returned to 91%; memcpy down from 7.3% -> 3.2%; average batch size dropped from 9.8 -> 6.1. Full logs: https://staging-pprofiles/redwood/exp/e-117
henry: that’s promising. Lower batch size + micro-tiles seems to pay off for this workload. Cost tradeoff looks like +8% token compute due to smaller batches but latency SLO regained.
maya: let's expand canary to 30% across other non-chat rerank nodes for 2 hours. If p95 stays within 3% of baseline, we keep it and add a follow-up to make kernel bias configurable per deployment tier.
sam: add TODO to perf board: "Make kernel_selector bias a runtime flag, expose per-route override, and add continuous-batcher metric for prefix entropy". Owner: @leah.
leah: taking it. I’ll open the PR for runtime flag + batcher change and schedule a roll plan. ETA EOD tomorrow. :white_check_mark: 
alex: thanks all — nice triage. I'll paste the expanded canary metrics once complete and include a short postmortem if anything odd pops up.
